newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's first corporate bond a smash hit--brokers.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's first corporate bond a smash hit--brokers.

text.p: Ghana's first registered corporate bond offer has been oversubscribed by 27 percent, brokers said on Monday.
Mortgage lending company Home Finance Co Ltd (HFC) raised $2,546,800 with the five-year bond, denominated in dollars and yielding seven percent. All applications have been accepted.
"The bonds have been well received, amongst others because HFC offered twice the interest rate banks pay for dollar accounts," Caroline Andah of New World Investments Ltd told Reuters.
The bulk of the bonds -- 88.5 percent -- went to institutions, as expected, brokers said.
The offer targeted insurance companies and multinational firms with local provident and pension schemes for employees.
About half of the bonds were paid for in cedis.

"The possibility of buying the bonds in cedis offers Ghanaians a possibility to hedge against the constant depreciation of their currency," Ken Ofori-Atta of lead manager Databank Financial Survices Ltd told Reuters.
Bonds may be redeemed after two years. Secondary trading on the Ghana Stock Exchange is to start on November 20, according to Ofori-Atta.
HFC is Ghana's top mortgage insitution. Six years ago it became the implementing agency for a $25 million housing finance scheme funded 60 percent by the state and 40 percent by the World Bank.

"HFC is a good vehicle of launching Ghana's long-term debt project. Long-term funds are crucial for development, without which our economy cannot grow," HFC managing director Stephanie Baeta Ansah told Reuters in an interview at the launching of the offer on September 18.

As in most developing countries, long-term credit is hard, if not impossible, to get in Ghana. Lacking confidence in the economy and in debtors, banks prefer to limit commitments to short- and medium-term loans.
